statement: The finite rational examples and constructed additive allocation in the handoff satisfy the stated demand and exchange checks.

validation: Run exact Fraction arithmetic over the specified finite subset domains; this checks examples only.

environment: Python 3 standard library; deterministic; no simulated empirical data

statement: Exact finite checks passed for C1, C2, C3, and a P6 case with negative and zero adjusted values; this is not a proof of general theorems.

supported_claim: Complete paper proof that the exchange axiom implies single-coordinate gross substitutes.
Complete paper proof that a modular fiscal transfer preserves the exchange axiom in both directions.
Complete paper proof of the two-worker exchange threshold and necessity for GS over all real prices.
Identity h=v+(q-v)=q establishes unrestricted set-contingent implementation of an EX target.
Complete paper proof for own-wage-separable, monotone effective costs and wage GS.
Complete paper proof by explicit wages and allocation for additive adjusted values.
Partial derivation: configuration LP duality and complementary slackness yield equilibrium conditional on an integral optimum; integrality remains unresolved.
Exact two-worker contingent-subsidy counterexample to GS.
Three-worker coverage-valuation counterexample showing submodularity does not imply GS.
Complete paper proof of discrete-concavity criterion for cardinality transfers on additive values.
The maximized objective is adjusted private value h=v+g and omits fiscal cost.
Government budget, information, and wage-dependent-policy equilibrium are outside the derived claims.
No Lean/Mathlib checker was run; no claim is formally proved.

statement: For every finite set valuation satisfying EX, demand satisfies single-coordinate and hence multi-coordinate GS over real prices.
Adding an employer-specific modular set transfer preserves EX in both directions and therefore preserves GS within the EX domain.

With two workers, adjusted value satisfies EX exactly when the fiscal cross-difference does not exceed the baseline substitutes slack; this is also necessary and sufficient for GS over all real prices.
For any baseline valuation and any EX target q, a set transfer g=q-v implements q and its GS demand; an additive target also has the P6 equilibrium.
uncertainty: Requires unrestricted, perfectly informed set-contingent transfers; no fiscal feasibility established

statement: An own-wage-separable fiscal rule with weakly increasing firm-specific effective costs preserves wage GS when its wage-independent adjusted value satisfies EX.
uncertainty: Demand result only; equilibrium existence with firm-specific nonlinear wage wedges is not established

statement: For additive adjusted employer values, the explicit maximum-value wages and assignment form a competitive equilibrium and maximize aggregate adjusted value.
uncertainty: General argument is a human paper proof; check run covers only a finite boundary instance

statement: Every finite EX adjusted-valuation market has a competitive equilibrium.
uncertainty: P7-O1 unresolved: exact integral-optimum theorem for the configuration LP under the stated EX assumptions has not been verified
unresolved_obligations: P7-O1: configuration LP integrality theorem and hypothesis match

statement: A positive contingent two-worker joint subsidy can destroy GS even when baseline value is additive.
uncertainty: Exact rational counterexample; no claim that equilibrium must fail

statement: Submodularity alone does not imply GS with three workers.

scope: finite additive baseline with cardinality-dependent transfer
statement: For additive baseline value plus cardinality transfer phi(|S|), EX holds exactly when phi has weakly decreasing discrete marginal increments.
uncertainty: Human proof covers all finite set sizes; check run covers only illustrative size four

statement: P6 establishes adjusted private-value maximization, not social welfare after government fiscal costs.
uncertainty: A welfare criterion and government budget have not been specified

statement: No theorem here establishes budget balance, information feasibility, or equilibrium under general wage-dependent taxes.
No model claim has Lean/Mathlib kernel verification.
